articles.title: Google data center head says that there are 'hundreds of thousands' of skilled trade jobs across the US as the company launches commitment to help 25,000 ...
articles.summary: Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers, as demand for
articles.body: Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers, as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the AI-driven data center boom. Tim Chadwick, Google’s Data Center Operations Area Lead, says there are “hundreds of thousands” of skilled trade jobs open across the country right now. Data centers have become central to the AI economy, requiring massive investment and labor. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the U.S., ranging from master electricians to project managers. These jobs offer long-term stability and high wages, but employers face challenges in recruiting due to decades of emphasis on four-year degrees over vocational training.A personal story behind the pushThe announcement was written by Tim Chadwick, Google's Data Center Operations Area lead for Ohio and Indiana, who shared his own path from military service into the tech industry. Chadwick spent seven years as a nuclear-trained operator in the US Navy and another 13 years as a submarine officer before transitioning to civilian life — a shift he described as genuinely difficult, one he credits his professional network with helping him navigate. A former shipmate ultimately helped him land an interview for a role managing data center engineering operations.Chadwick noted that many of the skills built while running a nuclear submarine — planning and leading a mission, working closely with technicians, and exercising sound judgment under pressure — translate directly into overseeing data center operations, a connection that shaped his interest in helping other veterans find similar paths.What the commitment includesGoogle.org's funding and support will flow to three organizations with deep experience serving the veteran community: Hiring Our Heroes, Student Veterans of America (SVA), and the Home Builders Institute (HBI). Together, these organizations will offer hands-on pre-apprenticeships, career coaching, and direct job placement support aimed at helping veterans and military family members move into skilled trade careers.Why the need is so urgentChadwick pointed to the sheer scale of unmet demand driving the initiative, noting that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently open across the US, spanning positions like master electrician, lead pipefitter, and project manager. He described these as high-growth careers offering long-term financial stability — and argued that veterans and military families are especially well-suited for them, given how closely the roles align with skills many already carry from military service, including problem-solving under pressure, teamwork, and a strong drive to get a job done right.Part of a broader pattern of investmentThis isn't Google's first move in this space. Earlier this year, the company joined BlackRock, Ford, and Carhartt to launch the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades, aimed at building stronger pipelines into vocational careers nationally. Google.org has also previously funded the Electrical Training Alliance (etA) to bring AI-powered learning tools directly onto the trade floor, and provided a $4 million grant to Student Veterans of America to expand access to Google Career Certificates and AI training for veterans nationwide.Today's announcement is also part of Google.org's broader AI Opportunity Fund for the United States, an initiative aimed at ensuring Americans across different career paths can benefit from advances in AI technology, rather than being left behind by them.You use AI every day. articles.title: DU college sets up panel to probe poll ‘malpractices’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Aditi Mahavidyalaya, a DU college, has formed a committee to investigate allegations of irregularities in its college-level elections after two
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Aditi Mahavidyalaya, a DU college, has formed a committee to investigate allegations of irregularities in its college-level elections after two candidates alleged discrepancies in counting, EVM handling and said that non-students, including a BJP functionary, were near a booth on the polling day.All the candidates who won the election on Sept 18 were backed by ABVP.On Sept 21, Diya Chhabra, who contested for president, and Prachi Wadhwa, who contested for secretary, sent a representation to the college, alleging election malpractice. The college informed them on Sept 24 that it had formed a probe committee.According to a result sheet that Chhabra and Wadhwa have submitted, 568 votes were cast across the two booths — 315 in booth 1 and 253 in booth 2. However, the number of votes recorded for the posts varied. For president, the total was 563 -- 314 in booth 1 and 249 in 2. For secretary, the votes cast were 539 -- 311 in booth 1 and 228 in booth 2. For the joint secretary post, 542 votes were cast -- the booth-wise break-up was 311 and 231.The duo said that while the shortfall was between one and four votes for president, the shortfall was 25 votes for secretary and 22 for joint secretary in booth 2. The two have asked how many NOTA votes were cast and asked for the unedited CCTV footage of polling day too.They also alleged that an observer in booth 1 was not allowed to stay inside the polling area and that EVMs were opened before voting without a verification by the candidates. A non-student, that too a man, was allowed on the women’s college campus during the campaign and the polling and was seen near a booth on Sept 18 between 11.30am and 1pm with BJP MLA Ravinder Indraj Singh, they wrote.When Singh was asked about this, he said that as a “public representative” he had gone to the campus. "The college is in my constituency, and I had got complaints about some commotion there.”The duo has approached Delhi High Court. “It is troubling that a college is alleged to have manipulated vote counts and allowed external political functionaries in,” counsel Shaurya Vikram said.Calls and texts to principal Neelam Rathi went unanswered.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: China introduces new homebuyer subsidies, encourages bank lending to boost property sector
articles.summary: China implemented fresh measures on Tuesday to support its economy and struggling property sector, as pressure builds ahead of the year-end deadline for
articles.body: China implemented fresh measures on Tuesday to support its economy and struggling property sector, as pressure builds ahead of the year-end deadline for meeting the government's growth target.The measures include encouraging targeted bank lending and introducing new subsidies towards homebuyers' mortgage interest payments.China’s central bank said it would cut the interest rate on its "pledged supplementary lending" facility, known as PSL, by a quarter of a percentage point, taking the one-year rate to 1.5 per cent.PSL is low-cost funding that the central bank provides to major state policy banks in order to back state and public projects.By reducing the rate, the bank said, it hopes to give lenders stronger incentives and to better "serve national strategies".The central bank will also raise the quota for relending aimed at technological innovation by 200 billion yuan (about USD 30 billion), lifting the total to 1.4 trillion yuan (USD 208 billion).Separately, the ministry of finance announced new mortgage interest subsidies for homebuyers.Starting in October, eligible first-time buyers can receive a subsidy equivalent to an annualised rate of one percentage point on the mortgage principal, for up to five years.To be eligible, the property must have a floor area of no more than 120 square metres (1,292 square feet) and a price of no more than 1.5 million yuan (USD 224,000).Gary Ng, a senior economist for Asia Pacific at the French bank Natixis, told Reuters that Tuesday's measures represent "a targeted approach with lower funding costs to support selected sectors through policy banks and the real estate sector".For the property market, Ng added, they aim "to support housing demand in lower-tier cities, which are still facing severe headwinds".Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 526 kg drugs worth Rs 3,000 crore seized from Iranian boat with Pakistani crew
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian Coast Guard, in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), seized approximately 526 kg of narcotics from an Iranian
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian Coast Guard, in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), seized approximately 526 kg of narcotics from an Iranian dhow in the Arabian Sea west of Lakshadweep, officials said.The Coast Guard said five Pakistani nationals operating the vessel were also detained during the operation carried out near Lakshadweep on September 25, as reported by news agency PTI.The drugs, valued at over Rs 3,000 crore in the international market, were seized after the vessel was intercepted during the operation.The Coast Guard conducted coordinated sea-air surveillance to track the suspicious vessel before launching a hot pursuit and boarding the dhow.The operation was carried out in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) to intercept the vessel. The seized contraband comprised heroin and methamphetamine, while five Pakistani nationals operating the dhow were also apprehended.The dhow, its crew and the seized drugs were escorted to Mumbai under armed security for joint interrogation and further legal proceedings.The operation was part of coordinated efforts by the Coast Guard and Gujarat ATS to detect and disrupt suspected transnational maritime drug-smuggling networks.The seizure comes as Indian maritime and law enforcement agencies continue efforts to prevent narcotics from being smuggled through sea routes. The Coast Guard has previously conducted joint operations with Gujarat ATS and other agencies to intercept vessels suspected of carrying illegal drugs.In April 2025, the Coast Guard, along with Gujarat ATS, seized 307.5 kg of narcotics off the Gujarat coast, according to the Coast Guard's official record of interdiction cases.Several drug-interdiction operations have been conducted along maritime routes in the Arabian Sea, with agencies relying on intelligence inputs, vessel surveillance and coordination between maritime and land-based enforcement units to identify suspected consignments.The Coast Guard said the latest operation underlined its efforts to strengthen maritime surveillance and prevent illicit activities in India's maritime zones. The seized drugs and apprehended crew were brought to Mumbai for further investigation and legal action.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Dr Strange in books, Sholay's Thakur in reality': Iran mocks UN over ‘inability’ to stop wars
articles.summary: Iran's embassy in India on Tuesday took a dig at the United Nations over its perceived failure to take decisive action in real-world conflicts, days after
articles.body: Iran's embassy in India on Tuesday took a dig at the United Nations over its perceived failure to take decisive action in real-world conflicts, days after Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi accused the global body of showing “indifference” to alleged violations of the UN Charter by the US and Israel.Click here for live updates on US-Iran warThe Iranian embassy shared a meme featuring two panels—one showing Marvel character Doctor Strange and the other depicting Thakur, played by Sanjeev Kumar in the 1975 Bollywood classic "Sholay."“UN according to school books,” read the caption on the first panel, which showed the multi-armed Dr Strange, a character known for his magical superpowers. The meme suggested that the UN is portrayed in textbooks as a powerful organisation capable of taking action on global issues.The second panel featured Thakur Baldev Singh, whose hands were amputated by the villain Gabbar Singh, played by Amjad Khan. Its caption read, “UN in reality,” suggesting that, in practice, the global body has been rendered "powerless" and unable to take effective action.Also Read | ‘Wake up’: Iran releases 25-page letter urging US voters to reject Trump ahead of midtermsIranian embassies have repeatedly used memes to mock the US and President Donald Trump amid the ongoing Middle East conflict, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran.Incidentally, Trump, too, has repeatedly criticised the UN since returning to office in January last year, accusing the organisation of being unable to resolve major global conflicts.Meanwhile, Araghchi met outgoing UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres in New York on the final day of his visit to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Iran's Tasnim news agency reported.During the meeting, Araghchi briefed Guterres on the latest developments in the Middle East and said Iran, “as a founding member of the United Nations,” expected the organisation and its member states to respond to what Tehran described as violations of international law and “blatant breaches” of the UN Charter by a permanent member of the Security Council, referring to the US.He also called for an "explicit" condemnation of what Iran described as US interventionist measures and “illegal threats” against the Islamic Republic.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Utah couple bought a 30-acre 'Lord of the Rings'-inspired estate in 2017, later added a pond, guesthouse and waterfalls; after a $5 million price cut, the 32-room property is now asking $38 million
articles.summary: A 30-acre estate in Provo, Utah, inspired by The Lord of the Rings, has received a $5 million price cut and is now listed for $38 million, Realtor
articles.body: A 30-acre estate in Provo, Utah, inspired by The Lord of the Rings, has received a $5 million price cut and is now listed for $38 million, Realtor reported. The 32-room property was previously asking $43 million. It includes a nearly 23,000-square-foot main house, a 6,200-square-foot guesthouse, a private pond, waterfalls, pools, sports facilities and private trails.The estate is set in the South Fork of Provo Canyon, among Utah’s ski mountains. Listing agent Kerry Oman of Summit Sotheby’s International Realty said there had been interest from potential buyers, but none had decided to purchase the property. “We had some good activity,” Oman said. “Some very capable candidates came in to see it, but it didn’t work for them.”The price was then reduced to make the property more attractive to buyers. “We decided to make it more enticing to buyers,” Oman said. “We wanted it to be enough (of a drop) so that people would notice.” He described the 30-acre estate as “one of the most remarkable properties anyone has ever seen in Utah” and said, “It’s really pretty spectacular.”The property was originally designed for an owner who wanted a home influenced by The Lord of the Rings. According to Oman, the original owner worked with architect Michael Upwall and Magleby Construction to create the design. The house was completed in 2014, with features inspired by the fictional world appearing throughout the property.A fantasy-inspired main houseThe main house measures 22,958 square feet and has six bedrooms, seven full bathrooms and three partial bathrooms. Its design combines stone, reclaimed wood and large glass walls, while several details draw directly from the fantasy-inspired theme.At the entrance, a porte-cochere features large circular openings described as “hobbit circles” leading towards the front door. The house also has circular fireplaces and windows, including a short hobbit-inspired door in one of the bedrooms.Inside, the architectural features include reclaimed barn wood, stone quarried in Utah, double-height timber walls, a winding staircase, a floating hallway and vaulted ceilings. A three-storey library and office is located on the main level.The property also makes extensive use of its mountain setting. Large glass walls and circular openings provide views of the surrounding landscape. Many rooms look towards Mount Timpanogos, the second-highest peak in Utah’s Wasatch Range.“Besides the design influence of ‘Lord of the Rings,’ everything is centered on the views,” Oman said.The lower level of the main house adds several recreational spaces. It includes a large games lounge, a theatre, a bunkroom, a golf simulator, a gym, indoor basketball and racquetball courts and a climbing wall measuring more than 50 feet.Pond, guesthouse and waterfallsThe estate was bought by Julie and Greg Cook in 2017. The couple later made major additions to the property. Oman said they added a large pond, a guesthouse and waterfalls in 2019-20.“In 2019-20, they added a large pond and the guest house and the waterfalls,” Oman said. “It really enhanced the property.”The 6,200-square-foot guesthouse has two bedrooms and sits over a private 1.5-acre pond. The pond has a dock, streams, waterfalls and natural stone diving platforms. The estate also has an outdoor pool, multiple patios and terraces, expansive lawns and private trails.The guesthouse is described as a two-bedroom lake house, adding another living space separate from the main residence. The property also includes an eight-car garage, an outdoor kitchen, covered dining and lounging areas, multiple fireplaces, a bar, a sauna and a hot tub.Together, the main house and guesthouse provide the estate's 32 rooms. The buildings sit on a 29.56-acre lot.Close to Provo and ski resortThe estate is located in the South Fork of Provo Canyon. Oman said it is about 15 minutes from Provo and close to skiing. “It’s a side canyon. You’re really close to skiing. It’s 25 minutes from the Sundance resort, but you’re up on a bench,” he said.The property is also about 30 minutes from private airports, according to Oman. He said it is around 45 minutes from Salt Lake City and about an hour from the airport there.Greg Cook is a co-founder and executive at DoTerra, which sells essential oils and other wellness products. The couple also founded several nonprofit organisations, including the Cook Center for Human Connection, founded in 2020.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Railway cancelled Katra train but withheld return fare; consumer court orders Rs 23,350 payout
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Sonipat district consumer commission has directed the railway board to refund Rs 7,350 to a passenger after it allegedly forfeited the fare
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Sonipat district consumer commission has directed the railway board to refund Rs 7,350 to a passenger after it allegedly forfeited the fare for his return train ticket when services to Katra were cancelled amid landslides during the Vaishno Devi pilgrimage in August 2025. The commission also awarded Rs 5,000 as compensation and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses. The order was passed on September 21, 2026.Why did the passenger approach the commission?According to the commission order, Baldev Raj Narang booked two train tickets for travel from New Delhi to Katra on August 31, 2025, and the return journey from Katra to New Delhi on September 1, 2025. The two tickets cost Rs 7,350 each, taking the total to Rs 14,700.The landslides on the Vaishno Devi pilgrimage routes led to the cancellation of the pilgrimage and railway services to Katra were also suspended. Narang therefore had to postpone his journey and sought a refund of the full Rs 14,700.The railway refunded Rs 7,350 for the New Delhi-Katra journey but did not refund the return-ticket amount. According to the order, the Railway alleged that the passenger had neither boarded nor cancelled the return ticket himself.Why did the commission say the return fare should also be refunded?The bench comprising president Vijay Singh and members Shyam Lal and Deepa Jain noted that railway records themselves showed that the return train had been cancelled.A message dated September 1, 2025, stated that train No. 12446 had been cancelled due to unavoidable circumstances, while another message dated August 31 also showed that the train had been cancelled due to operational reasons.The commission also noted that the railway later informed the passenger that the train had become operational only about six hours before its scheduled departure.“However record reveals that OP send another message to complainant regarding cancellation of train is now operational but only 6 hours before schedule time but in such a short span of time, it was not possible for complainant to bound the train from Katra,” the commission said.The commission added that restoring the train at such short notice could not justify withholding the passenger's money.“The evidence produced by complainant Annexure C-1 to C-6 proves that OP is deficient in service & unfair trade practices by not refunding the whole amount to the complainant,” it further held.The commission also noted that the passenger had submitted several requests for a refund but the railway failed to return the remaining amount. It said that since both sides of the journey had been affected by the cancellation, the passenger could not be blamed for not undertaking the return journey.What did the consumer commission order?The Sonipat district consumer commission allowed the complaint and directed the Railway Board to:Refund Rs 7,350 to the passenger from the date of filing of the complaint until actual realisation.Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental, physical and financial harassment.Pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.Comply with the order within 45 days of receiving the certified copy.The commission also directed that if the refund is not made within the prescribed period, the Rs 7,350 amount will carry simple interest at 8 percent per annum.

articles.title: Student protests rock France with over 400 detained: Why are schools protesting - explained
articles.summary: France was hit by a nationwide wave of strikes and student protests, with civil servants walking off the job and high school students blocking hundreds of
articles.body: France was hit by a nationwide wave of strikes and student protests, with civil servants walking off the job and high school students blocking hundreds of schools as anger over budget cuts, overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages spread across the country.The mobilisation came two days before Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's government is due to present its draft 2027 budget, which includes a planned €54 billion savings drive. The protests have added to pressure on the government as it tries to rein in France's finances ahead of next year's presidential election.The unrest was particularly visible at schools, where students piled up bins and barriers to prevent access. The education ministry said around 400 schools were affected by protests or disruptions on Tuesday, out of roughly 3,700 nationwide. More than 440 people, most of them minors, were detained, according to interior minister Laurent Nuñez.​​At least 10 teachers, several students and 48 law enforcement officers were also injured during Tuesday's unrest, according to officials.Students take protests beyond ParisThe school protests began in the Paris region last week but have since spread to cities including Lille, Lyon, Nantes, Marseille, Bordeaux and Rennes.Students have been protesting over a shortage of teachers, overcrowded classrooms, poor school conditions and demanding timetables. At some schools, however, the demonstrations escalated into clashes with police.In Lille, rubbish bins were set on fire outside the Lycée César Baggio, while police used tear gas and batons after protesters threw objects. Similar confrontations were reported elsewhere, although many blockades remained peaceful.At the Lycée Arago in Paris, students blocked the entrance with bins while a placard reading "Macron explosion" was displayed. Outside the Hélène-Boucher school, protesters put up a banner saying "Fewer cops, More money"."We want fewer police because we think there is a huge amount of police repression, both against high school student movements and social movements more generally," final-year student Mael Breton told Reuters.Students have cited teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and poor school conditions as key grievances. “There are 34 of us in each class, and it’s just not feasible. The teachers are overworked,” a 16-year-old student told AFP, saying the education system was “completely broken.”The government's response has been mixed. Lecornu condemned violence around schools but acknowledged that students' concerns over the education system needed to be heard and addressed. Education minister Édouard Geffray said students had a right to protest but condemned violence as "indefensible".Civil servants join nationwide strikeThe student mobilisation coincided with a broader strike by public-sector workers, including teachers, healthcare workers and firefighters.Unions organised more than 170 rallies across France to oppose the government's budget plans and its proposed freeze on state employees' base salaries in 2027. The CGT union has argued that repeated pay freezes have eroded workers' purchasing power.Firefighters were among those taking part after a summer of major wildfires exposed concerns over resources. The education ministry said just over 11% of teachers and other school staff were on strike, while participation among other civil servants was below 10%.Transport disruption was limited in the morning, although the aviation regulator warned of possible disruption at some airports.CGT leader Sophie Binet said the government had 48 hours to reverse the planned spending cuts before the union considers further strike action."This summer, who was on the front line? It wasn't the billionaires, the big bosses or the shareholders. It was civil servants and working people. And how are they being thanked? By cutting their pay? The anger is enormous," she told BFMTV.Why the budget is at the centre of the angerLecornu's government is trying to find savings as France grapples with a mounting debt burden. The proposed €54 billion savings package is aimed at bringing the public deficit down, while the government has also warned that public debt could reach 121.7% of GDP in 2027.France's public debt reached €3.595 trillion at the end of June, or around 119% of GDP, according to national statistics agency Insee.The cost of servicing that debt is also rising. France is expected to spend around €79 billion on interest payments this year, with the government projecting the figure could rise to €91 billion in 2027.The government is therefore trying to cut spending while unions resist pay restraint and students demand more teachers and resources for schools.You use AI every day. articles.title: They danced at prom in 1953, married others and reunited decades later: Joyce and Jim’s love story comes full circle
articles.summary: Some love stories take a long, winding path before they find their way home. In South Bend, Indiana, one such story has just come full circle.
articles.body: Some love stories take a long, winding path before they find their way home. In South Bend, Indiana, one such story has just come full circle. Joyce Kevorkian and Jim Bowman first danced together at their high school prom in 1953.Back then they were just teenagers having a good time. Decades later, after living full lives with other partners, they found their way back to each other and said “I do” in a quiet ceremony that felt like it had been waiting all along.A night to remember in 1953Joyce and Jim went to prom together more than sixty years ago. They have always said it was nothing serious at the time. According to CBS News, they were young, the evening was fun, and that was enough. After the dance they drifted apart the way so many high-school couples do.Each married someone else and built a life. Years passed. Careers, families, and everyday responsibilities filled their days. The prom night became a distant memory, the kind you smile about when an old photo turns up in a drawer.Letters, loss, and a second chanceLife eventually brought them both to the same quiet place. Fifty years after that prom, Joyce and Jim had each lost the spouses they had shared their lives with. One day Jim decided to write Joyce a letter. What started as a simple note turned into phone calls and conversations that felt surprisingly easy.The years seemed to melt away. Before long, Jim asked the question that changed everything. Joyce remembers the moment clearly. “I remember you said on the phone ‘will you marry me?’ And I said ‘that’s a good idea.’” There was no long speech or grand gesture, just two people who already knew the answer.A spark that never fully went outJim has a simple way of explaining what happened. “Getting together was meant to be,” he said. “They say a person never forgets their first real love and it was like there was a spark that was still smoldering in each of our hearts.”That quiet spark is what carried them through the decades. It stayed buried under the ordinary work of living, yet it never completely went cold. When the time was right, it was still there, ready to catch flame again.A quiet wedding and a new beginningThey kept the wedding small. Just a handful of close friends and family gathered to watch them exchange vows. There was no big production, only the two of them after so many years. Not long after the ceremony they returned from their honeymoon, still smiling at the strange and wonderful turn their lives had taken.For Joyce and Jim, the story is not about destiny written in the stars. It is about two people who once shared a single night of dancing, went their separate ways, and somehow found their way back when the moment was right. In a world that moves so fast, their silent meeting feels like a reminder that some bonds don’t completely disappear.

articles.title: Watch: Students protest in Odisha over textbook errors; national highway blocked
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Students and members of farmers' and youth organisations staged protests in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday as a 12-hour statewide Odisha bandh was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Students and members of farmers' and youth organisations staged protests in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday as a 12-hour statewide Odisha bandh was observed over alleged errors in school textbooks and a demand for the resignation of school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond.Members of the Naba Nirman Krushak Sangathan (NNKS) and Nabnirman Yuva Chhatra Sangathan (NYCS) blocked a national highway at Baramunda bus stand and torched tyres during the protest. Visuals from the protest showed demonstrators occupying the road as traffic movement was disrupted.The NNKS has called the bandh over what it described as large-scale errors in textbooks used in government schools. The organisation has been holding a relay hunger strike since August 20 and said the agitation would remain peaceful. NNKS national coordinator Akshay Kumar has been on hunger strike in Bhubaneswar since September 6.Speaking to ANI, M D Manwar Ali, state convenor of the Nabnirman Yuva Chhatra Sangathan, said the bandh had begun across the state."Right now, the Odisha Bandh is happening in Bhubaneswar at Baramunda. On that side is Hanspal, on this side is Uttara. Accordingly, across Odisha—whether West Odisha, East Odisha, or South Odisha—you will see picketing has started everywhere."What is the textbook row about?The NNKS claimed that more than 1,700 errors had been identified in newly published school textbooks, while NYCS alleged that the number was more than 2,000 in books for Classes 1 to 8. Among the examples cited were a reference to the Niyamgiri Hills as being in Jharkhand and a picture of the Karnataka assembly being used instead of the Odisha assembly. The organisations also alleged that scientist Isaac Newton was described as a pilot.Ali alleged irregularities in the textbook preparation process and claimed corruption worth Rs 380 crore. "Demanding the resignation of Odisha’s Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond, we have called for an Odisha Bandh today. We request everyone to support this call. In Odisha, for children's school textbooks from Class 1 to Class 8, there are more than 2,000 errors and a corruption of ?380 crore has taken place," he said.The organisations said they had received no response from the government despite their protests. "Therefore, today our demand is that Odisha’s Mass Education Minister must resign. Today marks 42 days of our protest. Our organisation’s founder Akshaya Ji has been on protest for 25 days, and today is my 18th day. articles.title: Coal worth ₹975 crore produced in violation of environmental norms in Odisha: CAG
articles.summary: CAG flags Odisha coal mines for producing 1.17 crore tonnes without valid environmental clearance or beyond limits; recoverable value of illegal coal estimated at ₹975.57 crore.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has flagged alleged violations of environmental-clearance norms in Odisha’s coal sector, stating that more than 1.17 crore tonnes of coal were produced beyond permissible limits or without a valid environmental clearance, making the lessee liable to pay ₹975.57 crore.In its compliance audit report for the year ended March 2024, CAG found irregularities in two coal mines operated by Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL). According to the audit, one mine exceeded the production limit permitted under its environmental clearance, while another continued production after the validity of its environmental clearance had expired.The larger violation was reported at Kalinga Open Cast Project under Talcher mining circle. The audit found that the mine’s environmental clearance expired in Oct 2021. Even after accounting for Covid-related extensions granted by Union environment ministry, the clearance remained valid only up to Oct 23, 2021. However, the mine continued coal production thereafter and extracted 1.15 crore tonnes of coal between Oct 2021 and March 2023 without a valid environmental clearance. The value of the coal produced during this period was assessed at ₹956.56 crore, the report stated.The audit observed that at Kulda Open Cast Project under Rourkela mining circle, the environmental clearance for coal production was enhanced from 19.6 million tonnes per annum to 21 million tonnes per annum in May 2022. However, based on the date of approval, the permissible production for 2022-23 worked out to 20.77 million tonnes on a pro-rata basis. Despite this, the mine produced 21 million tonnes, exceeding the permitted level by 2.3 lakh tonnes. CAG estimated the recoverable value of the excess production at ₹19.02 crore.Citing provisions of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, CAG said the lessee was liable to pay the value of the mineral extracted without lawful authority. Together, the violations in the two mines involved 1,17,96,540 tonnes of coal, attracting a recoverable amount of ₹975.57 crore.The audit also criticised the mining authorities for not adequately verifying the validity of environmental clearances and production limits while assessing mining operations. In the case of Kalinga OCP, Deputy Director of Mines, Talcher, “did not check the validity of EC and lawfulness of the production from the mine”, the report noted.When the audit pointed out the irregularities, the concerned deputy directors of mines stated that compliance would be furnished after verification of records.
